method.method_draft: Use a direct angle chase in the small triangle BDE. Read that D lies on AB and E lies on BC, so ray BD is along BA and ray BE is along BC. From the given angles in triangle ABC, compute angle B = 180° - 55° - 75° = 50°. Therefore angle DBE = 50°. Since DB = BE, triangle DBE is isosceles with vertex angle at B, so its two base angles are equal. Thus angle BED = (180° - 50°) / 2 = 65°.

method.method_draft: Use a coordinate/vector model centered at B. From triangle ABC, first compute angle ABC = 50°. Let B be the origin, and let the rays toward A and C form a 50° angle. Since D and E lie on these two rays and DB = BE, set D = r u and E = r v for unit vectors u and v with angle(u, v) = 50°. Then angle BED is the angle between vectors EB = -r v and ED = r(u - v). Using the dot product, cos(angle BED) = [(-v) · (u - v)] / |u - v| = (1 - cos 50°) / sqrt(2 - 2 cos 50°) = sin 25° = cos 65°. Hence angle BED = 65°.

Point D lies on side AB, point E lies on side BC, and segment DE is drawn. The marked angles are ∠A = 55° and ∠C = 75°. Reasoning: First compute ∠ABC = 180° - 55° - 75° = 50°. Use a coordinate/vector model centered at B. Let B be the origin, and let the ray from B toward A have unit vector u while the ray from B toward C has unit vector v. Then the angle between u and v is 50°. Since D is on BA, E is on BC, and DB = BE, write D = r u and E = r v for some r > 0. The angle ∠BED is the angle between EB and ED. We have EB = B - E = -r v and ED = D - E = r(u - v). Thus cos(∠BED) = [(-r v) · r(u - v)] / (|-r v| |r(u - v)|) = (1 - u·v)/|u - v|. Since u·v = cos 50°, this becomes (1 - cos 50°)/sqrt(2 - 2 cos 50°). Using identities 1 - cos 50° = 2 sin²25° and sqrt(2 - 2 cos 50°) = 2 sin25°, the ratio is sin25° = cos65°. Therefore ∠BED = 65°.
